target_customer: Individuals and developers who want a personal AI assistant or portable memory layer across AI tools (open source, self-hostable)
problem: AI assistants forget user context and cannot act proactively across apps; CORE keeps a user-owned memory graph shared with AI tools and apps.
business_model: Open source with hosted offering (monetization not found)
product_category: AI memory layer and personal assistant

founders.name: Manik Aggarwal
prior_employers: Velocity (senior product manager; grew Velocity Insights to 1,500 companies)
American Express (data scientist, credit risk models)

founders.name: Manoj Koncha
founders.background_notes: Engineering leader with 7+ years per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Memory graph for LLMs and integrations with many apps; the company posted an 88.24% LoCoMo memory-benchmark result in 2025, indicating real retrieval work.

defensibility.rationale: Open-source code can be forked and memory layers are a hot, copyable category; lock-in would come only from accumulated user memory.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too uncertain: mem0 raised $24M (seed and Series A, late 2025), Letta raised $10M (Sept 2024) and model vendors added built-in memory; dates are after the S23 batch.

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand from 2023 was found; the 2025 launch posts claim a benchmark result and positions CORE as a user-owned memory layer.

branding.domain_note: Company site getcore.me (not core.com); an earlier site and DEV org were heysolhq.

brand_strength.rationale: Short word fits a memory 'core', but extremely generic: search results for 'CORE' are dominated by CoreOps.AI, Coreworks and others; the YC slug is heysol, showing the earlier Sol branding. No community evidence beyond HN and DEV launch posts.

outcome_analysis: HeySol started as Sol, an AI personal assistant, and surfaced CORE, an open-source memory graph, in mid-2025; the YC listing now uses the CORE name with a three-person team in Bengaluru. No funding, customer figures or exit were found, and the directory's founding year (2025) conflicts with the Summer 2023 batch, so the record is thin. It competes with better-funded memory-layer startups such as Mem0 (raised $24M in late 2025) and Letta.
notes: No funding found anywhere. YC page shows batch Summer 2023 but founded 2025, so founded_year is left null.
